ranked_pipeline.headline: The Folk Wisdom of Trading Is Backwards
ranked_pipeline.subhead: When contenders buy from rebuilders — the trope every analyst assumes works — both sides underperform. Symmetric trades, where both teams sit on the same side of contention, generate twice the surplus.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: Symmetric trades: $6.4M surplus per trade. Asymmetric contender-vs-rebuilder: $3.1M. Gap $3.34M, t=4.99, p<0.0001.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Defies the most common framing in MLB trade analysis. Big counter-intuitive bombshell.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Front offices should re-examine their willingness to deal with peer contenders — the partner-contention-status filter is exactly backwards.

ranked_pipeline.headline: The $5M GM Gap
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Across 41 GMs with 40+ trades, the top quartile generates $7.0M of surplus per deal. The bottom quartile: $2.0M. Bootstrap CI on the gap [$3.71M, $6.28M].
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: Top quartile (Hill, Preller, Mozeliak, Luhnow, Rizzo, Beane, Anthopoulos, Cashman, Neander, Silverman) vs bottom (Coppolella, Minasian, Krall, Elias, Bridich). +0.55 WAR/trade, p=4.5e-9.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Named winners and losers. FanGraphs readers will share this with their tribal allegiances.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: A reputational ranking grounded in 14 years of dollar surplus is itself a competitive intelligence asset.

ranked_pipeline.headline: The Edge Isn't in the Farm — It's at the Margin
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Decompose the top-vs-bottom GM gap and the result is uncomfortable: every prospect-side feature is noise. The differentiator is acquired-player quality at the budget margin — top GMs pay more, for better players, more often.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: Acquired player quality: p=0.003 separates top vs bottom. Max FV / MiLB metrics / dev-cluster: all p>0.32.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Industry-shaking framing — the cliché 'win the trade by scouting' is wrong in aggregate. Pairs perfectly with the GM ranking piece as a two-part series.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Direct implication for FO process: spend the marginal evaluation hour on big-league acquisition selection, not prospect grading. This is a procurement-strategy article disguised as analysis.

ranked_pipeline.headline: The Prospect Stat That Pays in Dollars and Bleeds in Rate Stats
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Acquiring prospects who are young-for-their-level generates real dollar surplus — but the same players post worse wRC+ deltas than older peers. The market is pricing the wrong direction depending on the metric.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: β=+0.041 on dollar_surplus (98.2% mass), β=−0.032 on wrc_delta (90.4% mass). Old-for-level: −0.09 WAR. On-level: +0.36 WAR.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Sign-flip paradox is reliable nerd bait — same finding as t003 (player quality) but on the prospect side.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Service-time arbitrage is real and underpriced; the trade-off is rate-stat regression that pencils out anyway.

ranked_pipeline.headline: The 33-Point Swing: Where Young Hitters Become Players
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Age-advantaged MiLB hitters gain +16 wRC+ when acquired by top-track-record hitter-development orgs. Same archetype at the lowest-track-record orgs: −17. A 33-point swing on identical talent.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: +16.3 wRC+ at top-quartile hitter-dev orgs vs −17.2 at bottom. Replicates on `org_hitter_xwoba_jump_3yr` and `org_dev_fit_hitting`.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: 33 points is a huge effect — every reader can name an org that 'always develops hitters.' This is the data proof.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Org-fit-aware trade valuation. The exact same prospect is worth materially more to org A than org B and the market doesn't price it.

ranked_pipeline.headline: The August Trap
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Pitchers acquired in August — the post-deadline waiver/PTBNL window — post the worst FIP, xFIP, and SIERA deltas in the calendar. Twice the deadline-window penalty, three times offseason.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: FIP +0.55, xFIP +0.51, SIERA +0.57. Cleanest seasonal pitching signal in the dataset.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: August trades have always been the orphan window — readers will love finally seeing them quantified.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Adverse selection — these are pitchers other teams already passed on. Discount any August pitcher acquisition by ~half a run of expected ERA.

ranked_pipeline.headline: The Career-Stage Sweet Spot
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Acquisitions aged 28-30 produce more WAR and more dollar surplus than any other career bucket — and the market doesn't price that.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: Age 28-30: 0.90 WAR, $8.4M surplus. Age 31+: 0.59 WAR, $4.1M. Age 34+: 0.30 WAR, negative surplus wins. p<0.0001 on three outcomes.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Concrete buying advice. Readers compare this to their team's deadline acquisition list.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Avoid 31+ acquisitions; the market consistently overpays.

ranked_pipeline.headline: FanGraphs Said What? Why FV Grades Are Noise in Trade Outcomes
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Across nine trade outcome metrics, FanGraphs FV grades on acquired prospects never clear 70% directional mass. Level-adjusted MiLB hitting performance clears 88% on four separate outcomes.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: MiLB hit quality: 91.3% mass on WAR Δ, 89.8% on xwOBA Δ, 88.5% on xFIP Δ. FV grade: never above 70% on any outcome.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Direct shot at FanGraphs on FanGraphs' home turf. Comments section gold.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Re-weight prospect evaluation toward level-adjusted production over scout grades — at least for trade-outcome forecasting.

ranked_pipeline.headline: Dev Orgs Aren't What You Think They Are
ranked_pipeline.subhead: Top hitter-development orgs improve slow bats by 9 xwOBA points. They erode high-barrel power hitters by 17 wRC+. The 'dev org' brand is a contact-and-discipline factory, not a power factory.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: Slow bats: +9 xwOBA at high-dev, −8 at low-dev. Power hitters: −17 wRC+ at high-dev, −4 at low-dev.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Reframes a widely-used term. Reveals the trade-off baked into 'good dev org' branding.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Don't send power hitters to contact-focused dev orgs. Don't pay a dev-org premium for power acquisitions.

ranked_pipeline.headline: The Rookie Manager Advantage
ranked_pipeline.subhead: First-year managers extract 35% more WAR from acquired players than veterans with 5+ years of tenure.
ranked_pipeline.headline_stat: Year-1 managers: 0.66 WAR/trade. Vet (5+y): 0.49. Bootstrap CI [0.029, 0.313]. Holds within every GM tenure phase.
ranked_pipeline.why_reader_clicks: Counter-intuitive — vets are supposedly better at managing personalities.
ranked_pipeline.win_value: Front offices considering a rookie skipper get a small but real integration premium.

investigate_further.headline: Reclamation works, ascendance regresses — at high K-development orgs
investigate_further.rationale: Pairs directly with already-published k-trajectory-split.json. Could become a follow-up that adds the org-fit moderator. Medium credibility (n=88).

investigate_further.headline: Q2 MiLB pitching prospects outperform Q4 elites
investigate_further.rationale: Low credibility, doesn't survive multivariate controls. Needs park-adjusted MiLB metrics before publication.
